To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the early depletion of CD69+ T cell subsets in the intestine of SIV infected macaques may contribute to the development of intestinal pathology and immune dysfunction in HIV infected patients.
CD69 expression patterns on T cells in the gut and blood of SIV-infected rhesus macaques are distinct from those of normal macaques.
the majority of intestinal CD4 T cells are CD69+ in uninfected macaque monkeys.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of immune responses in the pathogenesis and treatment of HIV/AIDS.
understanding the role of the intestinal immune system in HIV/SIV infection.
the role of CD69 in the intestinal immune system, and the effects of HIV/SIV infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CD69+CD8+ T cells were the major early responders in SIV-infected rhesus macaques, and their selective depletion may have profound effects in the development of AIDS.
CD69 expression on T cells in mucosal tissues is different from that seen in the blood and lymphoid tissues, and this difference is lost during early SIV infection.
the expression of CD69 in intestinal lymphoid tissue of rhesus macaques is distinct from that of systemic lymphoid tissues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD69 expression is highly tissue-specific in normal rhesus macaques and that CD69 expression in intestinal tissues is markedly altered in early SIV infections.
we found that the CD69+CD3+ T cell population in the intestinal lamina propia of normal rhesus macaques is composed primarily of CCR5+ memory cells that express CD69.
CD69 is a key marker of T cell activation and may play a major role in the pathogenesis of HIV and SIV infections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CD69 is a marker for activated T cells in the gut, but not in the peripheral blood, lymph nodes, or spleen of uninfected macaque.
CD69 is a major marker for T cells in the intestinal lamina propia that are highly susceptible to SIV infection, but are not susceptible in systemic lymphoid tissues.
CD69 is expressed by memory CD4+ T lymphocytes in the intestine, and that these cells are a major target for SIV infection.
